> **What this case shows** — grouped by an expert's overnight sleep scoring, the
> ecosystem recovers the textbook **per-stage EEG spectra**: deep sleep (**N3**)
> is the slowest, most **delta**-dominated spectrum (relative delta **0.92**),
> the spectrum slows step by step as sleep deepens (**N1 < N2 < N3**), and stage
> **N2** carries the **sleep-spindle** peak in the sigma band — and all of this
> **reproduces across two independent nights**. **What reproduces, and what
> doesn't** — the *spectral fingerprints* reproduce; the tool's built-in
> one-threshold *auto-stager* does **not** match the expert hypnogram (agreement
> **9 % / 5 %**), because on these frontal, delta-heavy home recordings a single
> cutoff collapses to "N3". So the ecosystem is trustworthy here as a **spectral
> measurement**, not as a finished automatic scorer. **How to read it** — left,
> relative delta power per stage (higher = slower/deeper), both nights; right,
> the spindle-band power that singles out N2.

::: {.callout-tip title="The recipe you'll learn"}
**Workflow** — answer *"what does each sleep stage look like spectrally?"* in
three moves: **load** the EEG derivations → **epoch + spectrally summarise** each
30 s window → **group** the per-epoch spectra by the expert stage labels and
compare.
**Way of thinking** — separate the two jobs a staging tool does: *measuring* the
per-epoch spectrum (reliable) and *classifying* it into a stage (hard — needs
artifact handling, more channels/features). Validate the measurement against the
ground-truth labels, and don't mistake a convenience classifier for a scorer.
**Ecosystem usage** — chain one function per role, I/O → analysis
(`readEDF` → `eegSleepStage`), letting the shared data model carry the signal.
The final section turns this into a step-by-step you can adapt to your own PSG.
:::

## Proposition

Grouped by the expert hypnogram, deep sleep (**N3**) is the most delta-dominated
spectrum (relative delta **0.92** night 1, **0.91** night 2 — the highest of all
five stages), the spectrum **slows monotonically as sleep deepens**
(relative delta **N1 < N2 < N3**), and **N2** carries the **sigma-band spindle
peak** — reproduced across both nights.

## Question & goal

**The question comes from the dataset's own design.** Sleep-EDF Expanded was
built for one task: **sleep staging** (Kemp et al., 2000). Each overnight
recording is divided into 30-second epochs and an expert scores every epoch into
**W / N1 / N2 / N3 / REM** — the *hypnogram* shipped with the data. Staging is
possible because each stage has a **spectral fingerprint**: deep slow-wave sleep
is dominated by low-frequency **delta**; stage N2 is marked by **sleep spindles**
(a burst in the ~12–16 Hz sigma band); lighter N1 and REM run faster, with more
theta and alpha. So we ask the dataset's own question from the measurement side:
does the ecosystem recover those per-stage spectra when we group its output by
the expert labels — and does it hold across nights?

## Challenge & approach

Two jobs hide inside "staging", and they earn trust separately: *measuring* each
epoch's spectrum, and *classifying* it into a stage. We validate the measurement.
The recipe reads the two EEG derivations, cuts the night into 30-second epochs,
and summarises each epoch's spectrum as band powers — then we group those spectra
by the expert stage and average:

```
readEDF(channels = c("EEG Fpz-Cz", "EEG Pz-Oz"))  →  eegSleepStage(epoch_sec = 30)
```

`eegSleepStage()` returns, per 30-second epoch, the relative power in each band
(delta, theta, alpha, sigma, beta) *and* a first-pass stage label. We take the
**band powers** as the per-epoch spectral features, group them by the epoch's
**expert** stage, and read off the fingerprints. The first-pass label is kept
only to show, honestly, how far a single-threshold classifier is from expert
scoring. Everything is deterministic, so it replays exactly.

## Data

**Sleep-EDF Database Expanded** (sleep-cassette), nights **SC4001** and
**SC4011** — public on PhysioNet
(<https://physionet.org/content/sleep-edfx/1.0.0/>), ODbL. Two frontal/occipital
EEG derivations (**EEG Fpz-Cz**, **EEG Pz-Oz**) at 100 Hz, with an expert
hypnogram per night. The exact recordings (with checksums) are listed in
[`artifacts/data_sources.json`](artifacts/data_sources.json); the hypnograms are
parsed for their stage labels only. *Kemp B, et al. IEEE Trans Biomed Eng.
2000;47(9):1185–94; Goldberger AL, et al. Circulation. 2000;101(23):e215–20.*

## Results

![Left: relative delta power by expert-scored stage for both nights — N3 (deep sleep) is the delta peak, and delta rises N1 < N2 < N3 as sleep deepens; wake (W) sits off the ladder. Right: relative sigma (spindle-band) power by stage — the sleep spindle singles out N2. Both signatures reproduce across the two nights.](artifacts/figure.png)

*How to read this:* each bar is a band's share of that epoch's total power,
averaged over all epochs the expert gave to that stage — so higher relative delta
means a slower spectrum, and the sigma bar is the spindle band.

**Per-stage spectra**
([`artifacts/stage_signature_SC4001.csv`](artifacts/stage_signature_SC4001.csv),
[`SC4011`](artifacts/stage_signature_SC4011.csv)):

| Stage | Rel. delta (N1) | Rel. delta (N2) | Rel. delta (N3) | Rel. sigma at N2 (spindle) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Night 1 (SC4001) | 0.629 | 0.818 | **0.922** | **0.020** |
| Night 2 (SC4011) | 0.725 | 0.795 | **0.911** | **0.028** |

In both nights N3 is the delta peak, delta climbs N1 → N2 → N3 (the spectrum
slows as sleep deepens), and the spindle band peaks in N2 — the fingerprints
staging relies on, recovered from the raw EEG.

**What does not reproduce**
([`artifacts/staging_agreement.csv`](artifacts/staging_agreement.csv)): the
built-in single-threshold classifier matches the expert hypnogram on only
**8.9 %** (night 1) and **4.8 %** (night 2) of epochs — on these frontal,
delta-dominated home recordings it labels almost everything N3. And **wake** does
not fit the depth ladder (relative delta ~0.81 / 0.85), because the frontal
Fpz-Cz derivation picks up eye movement and muscle activity while the subject is
awake. The measurement is trustworthy; turning it into a scorer is a separate,
harder problem.

## Conclusion

Grouped against expert hypnograms, the ecosystem recovers the canonical spectral
fingerprints of sleep — N3's slow-wave delta dominance, the N1 → N2 → N3 slowing,
and the N2 spindle — reproducibly across two nights. The transferable lesson is
to **separate measuring from classifying**: validate that your tool measures the
per-epoch spectrum correctly against ground-truth labels before trusting anything
built on top of it, and report the classifier's real agreement rather than
implying the labels are as good as an expert's.

## Open questions

The convenience classifier in `eegSleepStage()` — a single relative-power
threshold — does not reproduce expert scoring on this ambulatory frontal montage
(agreement < 10 %). Whether artifact rejection plus richer features and more
channels would recover clinical-grade automatic staging is a genuine question,
but building an automatic scorer is beyond this case. Documented, not escalated.

## Using this in your own analysis

This case is a worked example of a **grouped spectral profile** — the pattern for
any "what does the spectrum look like in each labelled state?" question, and a
template for **validating a measurement against ground-truth labels**.

**The general recipe** (three steps):

1. **Load** the channels where the signal lives — here the two Sleep-EDF EEG
   derivations.
2. **Epoch and spectrally summarise** with `eegSleepStage()`, which returns
   per-30-second band powers (and a first-pass label).
3. **Group by the true labels** — your expert hypnogram — and average each band
   within a stage to read off the fingerprint; check it against known physiology.

**Which functions, and how they compose.** Each step is one ecosystem function,
picked by *role* — I/O → analysis:

| Step | Function | Package |
|---|---|---|
| load the PSG EEG derivations | `readEDF()` | PhysioIO |
| per-30 s band powers + first-pass stage | `eegSleepStage()` | PhysioEEG |
| (related) detect the spindles themselves | `eegSpindleDetect()` | PhysioEEG |

They chain because `eegSleepStage()` consumes the `PhysioExperiment` that
`readEDF()` returns — the shared data model connects I/O to analysis, so you
compose by naming the steps.

**Choosing the parameters.**

- **Channels** — staging uses central/occipital EEG; here Fpz-Cz + Pz-Oz. A more
  central montage and adding EOG/EMG derivations improves stage *separation*
  (and is what expert scoring uses).
- **`epoch_sec = 30`** — the AASM scoring epoch; keep it at 30 s to align with
  standard hypnograms.
- **Read the *relative* bands, not absolute power** — relative band power compares
  spectral *shape* across stages and is robust to the montage/impedance drift
  that shifts absolute scale.

**Applying it to your own hypothesis.** Swap in your own scored PSG (or any
signal with per-epoch labels), keep the load → epoch-spectra → group-by-label
recipe, and compare the fingerprints across conditions or groups. The same
"group a spectral feature by state" logic is exactly the eyes-open/closed
contrast on wake EEG ([`eeg-berger-eegmmidb`](../eeg-berger-eegmmidb/)); the
validate-against-ground-truth logic mirrors the beat-detector benchmark on ECG
([`ecg-qrs-benchmark-mitbih`](../ecg-qrs-benchmark-mitbih/)).

**The recipe, copy-runnable:**

```r
library(PhysioIO); library(PhysioEEG)

# 1. load the two EEG derivations from the polysomnogram
pe <- readEDF("SC4001E0-PSG.edf", channels = c("EEG Fpz-Cz", "EEG Pz-Oz"))

# 2. per-30 s relative band powers (delta, theta, alpha, sigma, beta) + a label
ss <- eegSleepStage(pe, method = "spectral", epoch_sec = 30)

# 3. group the band powers by your expert hypnogram stage and average
#    -> N3 is the relative-delta peak; the sigma band peaks in N2 (spindles)
stages   <- read_hypnogram_labels("SC4001EC-Hypnogram.edf")  # your parser
ss$stage <- stages[ss$epoch]
aggregate(cbind(delta_power, sigma_power) ~ stage, data = ss, FUN = mean)
```

**Auditing the numbers.** For readers who want to verify rather than trust: the
per-epoch aligned spectra, the per-stage fingerprints, and the classifier
agreement live in [`artifacts/`](artifacts/), and `audit.py` re-derives every
number on this page — the per-stage means, the four canonical orderings in both
nights, and the agreement figures — from those files.
